title: GcArticleRecord and GcCandidate are parallel types never joined in production
description:
## Why this issue exists

Two structurally identical types exist across the GC subsystem with no conversion between them and no production code that joins them:

- `GcArticleRecord` (gc_candidates.rs): returned by `select_gc_candidates`, which already filters by policy
- `GcCandidate` (gc.rs): consumed by `GcRunner::run_once`, which re-evaluates policy on the same candidates

`select_gc_candidates` evaluates `policy.should_pin` to exclude pinned articles, then returns `GcArticleRecord`. `GcRunner::run_once` takes `&[GcCandidate]` and also evaluates `policy.should_pin`. Policy is evaluated twice on the same data.

There is no `From<GcArticleRecord> for GcCandidate` or any other conversion. No production path in main.rs calls `select_gc_candidates` and passes the result to `run_once` — the two halves exist only in their own tests.

## What needs to be done

Either:
1. Merge into one type (`GcCandidate` or `GcArticleRecord`), remove the duplicate policy evaluation, and wire the production path in main.rs
2. Add `impl From<GcArticleRecord> for GcCandidate` so the seam is explicit and the compiler enforces that field additions propagate

The real fix is option 1: the policy evaluation in `select_gc_candidates` should be removed (let the DB query return all out-of-grace-period articles), the two types should be merged, and `run_once` or the scheduler wrapper becomes the single policy evaluation point.
